instructions: Does the latest message from the contact need a reply from the dental clinic?

criteria.yes: The contact asks something, requests something or expects an answer.
criteria.no: A closing, thanks or acknowledgement that needs no reply.

instructions: Should a person from the clinic take over instead of the automated assistant? Yes if the contact asks for a human, complains or is upset, is distressed or stuck asking for help, asks for clinical advice that only a professional can give (what to take, whether something is serious, what to do about a symptom, test results), or describes an emergency that may put a life at risk: chest pain, trouble breathing, bleeding that does not stop, a swollen face, swelling that blocks breathing or swallowing, high fever in a baby, fainting, an accident. No if the contact mentions a symptom, even strong pain, to ask where or when they can be seen, for an appointment, a price or availability: the assistant offers the nearest visit.
How urgent is the latest message from the contact?

levels.label: low
levels.description: No time pressure: general information or a routine request.

levels.label: medium
levels.description: Needs attention today: wants an appointment soon, follow-up or a change.

levels.label: high
levels.description: Needs attention now: pain, bleeding, swelling, accident or distress.

instructions: What is the main intent of the latest message from the contact?

options.description: Wants to book an appointment or asks what dates or times are available.
Wants to move or cancel an existing appointment.

Asks for general information about the clinic or how it works: prices, treatments offered, locations, hours, payment methods, instalments, insurance, parking, whether walk-ins are accepted or what to bring. A question to answer, not a request to book or to do something for them.

Asks for clinical advice (what to take, whether it is serious, what to do about a symptom) or describes an emergency. Mentioning a symptom while asking for an appointment, a price or availability is not this: choose that request.
Complains about the service or the clinic.
Greeting, thanks or closing with no request.

Unrelated to dental care, the mouth or the clinic: cooking, homework, programming, sports, politics, general knowledge, translations, writing texts or jokes. Never use it for anything about teeth, the mouth, eating or care after a dental procedure, the clinic's services, prices, payment, insurance, paperwork, access or appointments.
None of the above or unclear.

instructions: Does the contact ask the clinic to stop sending messages?

Is the latest message from the contact spam: unsolicited advertising, a scam, a chain message, an automatic reply from another business, or a company selling something to the clinic? A person writing for themselves is never spam.

options.description: A person writing for themselves: about teeth, the mouth, the clinic, appointments, prices, payments, a complaint, a greeting, a wrong number or anything personal. When in doubt, choose this.
Mass advertising or offers from others: earn money, loans, investments, products or promotions.
Fraud or phishing: asks to pay or click a link for a package, prize, bank, account or delivery.
A chain message that asks to forward it to other people.
An automatic reply or bot of another business: thanks for writing, we will reply soon; away messages; menus.
A company or agency offering its products or services to the clinic: websites, marketing, software, supplies or laboratories.
